narrative: Global markets are under pressure as heavy big-tech AI infrastructure capital expenditures trigger intense scrutiny and position unwinding following weak guidance from Intel, Alphabet, and Amazon. Concurrently, US midterm elections are approaching with consensus expecting a Republican flip of the House, raising prospects of legislative gridlock, congressional investigations, and regulatory battles over AI data centers. Geopolitical risks are intensifying across multiple theaters, with potential US-Israel military action against Iran threatening crude transit in the Strait of Hormuz, alongside Ukrainian drone strikes hitting Russian refineries. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve has held interest rates steady, but persistent cost-push inflation in fuel, food, and mortgages keeps rate policy uncertain ahead of December. Emerging markets are also reeling, highlighted by a severe crash in Brazilian equities and the real following the presidential election.

Nasdaq.why: Michael Ball notes the index plunged 3.5% as crowded hyperscaler longs unwound over concerns regarding AI capex returns, traditional business softening, and semiconductor guidance cuts. Blair Effron adds that local backlash and data center moratoriums present mounting structural headwinds.

S&P 500.why: The index fell 1.8% to breach its 100-day moving average under tech pressure and geopolitical anxiety, as noted by anchors and Ethan Bronner. While Steven Rattner and Benton Graham point to multi-year strength and resilient consumer spending, defensive rotations have only partially cushioned headline downside.

Gold.why: Ethan Bronner and anchors highlight that elevated safe-haven demand is strongly supported by mounting US-Israel-Iran escalation risks, deadlocked Israeli elections, and intensifying conflict in Ukraine.

Oil.why: Nathan Dean, Ethan Bronner, and Jason Furman warn of acute upside supply risks stemming from potential military strikes on Iran disrupting the Strait of Hormuz, compounded by Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refining capacity.
